topics.label: Evolution
facts: Evolution is the change in living things over many generations.
Charles Darwin explained evolution by natural selection: living things with helpful traits are more likely to survive and have young.
Fossils show that life on Earth has changed over millions of years.
All living things on Earth share a common ancestor from long ago.

choices: Change in living things over many generations
questions.fact: Evolution is how species change slowly over many generations.

questions.q: Who explained evolution by natural selection?
questions.fact: Darwin showed that helpful traits are passed on because their owners survive and reproduce.

questions.q: What do fossils tell us about evolution?
choices: That life on Earth has changed over millions of years
questions.fact: Fossils record how species appeared, changed, and sometimes died out over time.

choices: Living things with helpful traits are more likely to survive and have young
questions.fact: Natural selection is nature favouring traits that help survival and reproduction.

topics.label: Genetics
facts: Genetics is the study of how traits are passed from parents to their children.
DNA is the molecule that carries the instructions for building a living thing.
Genes are sections of DNA that control traits like eye colour.
You get half of your DNA from each of your parents.

choices: The study of how traits are passed from parents to children
questions.fact: Genetics explains why children often look like their parents.

questions.q: What molecule carries the instructions for building a living thing?
questions.fact: DNA holds the instructions for making every part of a living thing.

choices: A section of DNA that controls a trait
questions.fact: Genes are stretches of DNA that carry instructions for traits like eye colour.

questions.q: How much of your DNA comes from each parent?
questions.fact: You inherit half your DNA from your mother and half from your father.

topics.label: Photosynthesis
facts: Photosynthesis is how plants make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts, the green parts inside plant cells.
During photosynthesis, plants make glucose, a sugar, and release oxygen.
Almost all life on Earth depends on photosynthesis, directly or indirectly, for food and oxygen.

choices: How plants make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
questions.fact: Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy stored in food.

questions.q: Where does photosynthesis happen in a plant cell?
questions.fact: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, the green pigment that traps sunlight.

questions.q: What do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which animals need to breathe.

questions.q: What sugar do plants make during photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Photosynthesis makes glucose, which plants use for energy and growth.

topics.label: The Human Brain
facts: Your brain is the control centre of your body, and it is protected by your skull.
The brain is made of about 86 billion nerve cells called neurons.
The largest part of the brain, the cerebrum, is where you think, remember, and make decisions.
Even though it is only about 2 percent of your body weight, your brain uses about 20 percent of your energy.

questions.fact: The skull is a hard case of bone that protects the brain.

questions.q: What are the brain's nerve cells called?
questions.fact: Neurons are nerve cells that carry messages in the brain and body.

questions.q: Which part of the brain helps you think and remember?
questions.fact: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and handles thinking and memory.

questions.q: About how much of your body's energy does your brain use?
questions.fact: The brain uses about a fifth of the body's energy, even though it is small.
